## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## drawer — Drawer (component, archetype navigate)
A panel that slides in from a screen edge, holding navigation, detail, filters or an assistant beside the main content.
Aliases: side sheet, flyout panel, slide-over
Anatomy: Panel (The drawer surface); Scrim (What covers content when modal); Handle or trigger (What opens it)
Related — neighbors: modal-dialog, bottom-sheet, split-pane
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Edge and relationship [layout] — Which edge, and does it cover, push or sit beside content?
  - edge (single-select: one id) — Edge
      left: Left (e.g. Navigation drawers)
      right: Right (e.g. Detail panels)
      top: Top (e.g. Notification shades)
  - relationship (single-select: one id) — Relationship to content
      overlay-with-scrim: Overlay with scrim (e.g. Material modal navigation drawer)
      push-content: Push content (e.g. Standard drawers)
      docked: Docked (e.g. Material standard side sheet)
      overlay-no-scrim: Overlay, no scrim — The panel lies over the content without dimming or disabling it visually (GitHub Projects item panel, Notion side peek, OS panels) (e.g. GitHub Projects — Item side panel)
* Contents [content] — What is it for?
  - holds (single-select: one id) — Holds
      navigation: Navigation (e.g. Gmail on Android)
      item-detail: Item detail (e.g. GitHub Projects item panel)
      filters: Filters (e.g. Mobile retail)
      settings: Settings (e.g. Admin consoles)
      assistant: Assistant (e.g. Microsoft Edge Copilot sidebar)
      system-status-and-controls: System status and controls — Notifications, quick toggles and widgets belonging to the OS rather than the app (Android shade, iOS Control Center, Windows Widgets, macOS Notification Center) (e.g. Android — Notification shade)
      companion-apps: Companion apps — Small versions of ot

## kanban-board — Kanban board (pattern, archetype browse-collections)
Items as cards in columns that stand for states or categories; moving a card between columns changes its value.
Aliases: board, task board, pipeline
Anatomy: Board (The whole set of columns); Column (A value of the grouping attribute); Card (One item’s key attributes); Swimlane (An optional second grouping across columns)
Related — uses: card, drag-reorder, filter-controls, modal-dialog, drawer, badge | specializes: overview-detail | neighbors: data-table, gantt-timeline
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Grouping [composition] — What do columns and swimlanes stand for?
  - columns (single-select: one id) — Column source
      workflow-status: Workflow status — Columns are workflow states (e.g. Jira board)
      any-single-select-field: Any single-select field — Group by a chosen property (e.g. Notion board, GitHub Projects)
      assignee: Assignee — One column per person (e.g. Linear grouped by assignee)
      manual-lists: Manual lists — Columns are free-form lists (e.g. Trello)
  - swimlanes (single-select: one id) — Swimlanes
      none: None (e.g. Trello)
      by-assignee: By assignee (e.g. Jira)
      by-parent-or-epic: By parent or epic (e.g. Jira swimlanes by epic)
      by-query: By query — Each lane is a saved filter (e.g. Jira query swimlanes)
      manual-lanes: Manual lanes — Free-named lanes the team defines (e.g. Expedite) into which cards are placed by hand, not derived from a field (e.g. Azure DevOps — Kanban board)
* Card and column content [content] — What does each card and column say about its items?
  - cardFields (multi-select: list of ids) — Card attributes
      title: Title (e.g. All boards)
      assignee-avatar: Assignee avatar (e.g. Jira)
      labels: Labels (e.g. Trello labels)
      due-date: Due date (e.g. Trello)
      estimate: Estimate (e.g. Jira story points)
      cover-image: Cover image (e.g. Trello card covers)
      sub-task-progress: Sub-task progress (e.g. Checklist progress in Trello)
      amount-or-value: Amount or value — A monetary or numeric value on the card that is the point of the board — deal size, contract value — distinct from an effort Estimate; columnSummary already names its total but cardFields has no way to say the card carries it (e.g. Pipedrive — Deals pipeline)
  - columnSummary (multi-select: list of ids) — Column summaries
      none: None (e.g. Trello)
      card-count: Card count (e.g. Most boards)
      wip-limit: WIP limit — A maximum, flagged when exceeded (e.g. Jira column constraints)
      sum-of-an-attribute: Sum of an attribute — Total estimate or value (e.g. Pipedrive deal value per stage)
* Transitions [flow] — What happens when a card moves?
  - transitions (multi-select: list of ids) — Transition rules
      free-movement: Free movement — Any column to any column (e.g. Trello)
      allowed-transitions-only: Allowed transitions only — The workflow forbids some moves (e.g. Jira workflows)
      required-fields: Required fields — A screen collects data on transition (e.g. Jira transition screens)
      automation-on-move: Automation on move — Moves trigger actions (e.g. Trello Butler, Jira Automation)
* Card size and columns [layout] — How are cards and columns sized and arranged?
  - cardSize (single-select: one id) — Card size
      compact: Compact — Title only (e.g. Linear compact board)
      default: Default — Title plus key fields (e.g. Jira)
      expanded: Expanded — Covers and descriptions (e.g. Trello with covers)
  - columnBehaviour (multi-select: list of ids) — Column behaviour
      horizontal-scroll: Horizontal scroll (e.g. Trello)
      collapsible-columns: Collapsible columns (e.g. Linear, GitHub Projects)
      fit-to-width: Fit to width (e.g. Small boards)
      one-at-a-time: One at a time — Only one column fills the screen at a time; swiping left or right moves to the adjacent column, e.g. Trello's mobile board (e.g. Trello — A b

## prompt-input — Prompt input (component, archetype delegate-ai)
The control where a person enters or edits the instruction, context and attachments sent to a model.
Aliases: composer, prompt box, AI text field
Anatomy: Text area (The instruction); Attachments (Files, images, selections); Submit (Send or run); Modifiers (Model, tools, parameters)
Related — neighbors: text-field, suggestion-chips, file-upload
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Input content [content] — What can the composer hold?
  - content (multi-select: list of ids) — Content
      plain-prompt: Plain prompt (e.g. ChatGPT box)
      mentions-of-files-or-symbols: Mentions of files or symbols (e.g. Cursor @)
      attached-images-or-docs: Attached images or docs (e.g. ChatGPT uploads)
      hidden-system-preamble: Hidden system preamble (e.g. Custom GPTs)
      parameter-flags: Parameter flags (e.g. Midjourney suffix)
* Composer layout [layout] — Where does the prompt UI sit?
  - layout (single-select: one id) — Layout
      bottom-sticky-composer: Bottom sticky composer (e.g. ChatGPT)
      inline-caret-popover: Inline caret popover (e.g. Cursor Cmd-K)
      modal-brief: Modal brief (e.g. Agent task dialogs)
      sidebar-composer: Sidebar composer (e.g. IDE chat panels)
      voice-first-with-transcript: Voice-first with transcript (e.g. Voice modes)
      centred-hero-box: Centred hero box — A large prompt box in the middle of an empty page that becomes the bottom composer once a thread starts (e.g. Perplexity — Ask anything box)
      terminal-prompt-line: Terminal prompt line — A readline-style input at the bottom of a terminal transcript, with slash commands and mentions typed in place (e.g. Claude Code — Prompt line)
* Submitting [invocation] — How is the prompt sent?
  - submitBy (multi-select: list of ids) — Submit by
      enter-key: Enter key (e.g. Chat UIs)
      click-send: Click send (e.g. All)
      push-to-talk: Push to talk (e.g. Voice)
      queue-while-running: Queue while running (e.g. Follow-ups mid-stream)
      schedule-send: Schedule send (e.g. Batch agents)
      open-mic: Open mic — Nothing is pressed or held to send — the microphone stays open and voice activity detection ends the turn, which is what separates modern voice modes from push-to-talk (e.g. ChatGPT — Voice mode screen)
* Composer assistance [initiative] — What help shapes the prompt before send?
  - assistance (multi-select: list of ids) — Assistance
      none: None (e.g. Bare text boxes)
      placeholder-examples: Placeholder examples (e.g. Chat onboarding)
      rewrite-my-prompt: Rewrite my prompt (e.g. Prompt improvers)
      suggestion-chips: Suggestion chips (e.g. Starter prompts)
      template-slots: Template slots (e.g. Fill-in briefs)

## activity-log — Activity log (pattern, archetype monitor)
A time-ordered record of what happened to an object or account, and who did it.
Aliases: audit log, history, changelog, event timeline
Anatomy: Event (One change); Actor (Who did it); Subject (What it happened to); Filters (Narrowing the record)
Related — uses: filter-controls, date-picker, accordion | specializes: monitor | neighbors: version-history, notification-center, feed
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Event detail [content] — How much does each event say?
  - detail (single-select: one id) — Detail
      one-line-summary: One-line summary (e.g. GitHub issue timeline)
      before-and-after-values: Before and after values (e.g. Jira history tab)
      full-diff: Full diff (e.g. Wiki page history)
      expandable-groups: Expandable groups (e.g. Google Docs activity)
* Subject [scope] — Whose activity is it?
  - subject (single-select: one id) — Subject
      one-object: One object (e.g. Issue history)
      a-workspace: A workspace (e.g. Admin audit logs)
      the-person-s-own: The person’s own (e.g. Google My Activity)
      the-whole-system: The whole system (e.g. AWS CloudTrail)

aesthetics.typography: Inter Variable for everything (headlines, body, UI mockups); Berkeley Mono for small uppercase captions ('POWERING THE COMPANIES…', 'FIG 0.1', changelog dates) and code in mockups
aesthetics.typeScale: Large tight-tracked display: 64px H1, 48px section H2s, 24px lead paragraphs, then dense 12–15px UI text and 10–11px mono captions; weights mostly 400–510, contrast carried by size and grey levels rather than bold

label.notes: Near-black (#08090a) Linear site with product UI rebuilt in live DOM rather than screenshots: hero issue view with agent panel, kanban, roadmap, scatter chart, agent panels and code diff, all slightly fading into the background with radial vignettes. Section pattern repeats: big 2-line heading left, grey lead copy right, 'Learn more →', full-bleed mockup, then a 'Features' row of '+' buttons that open a right-side 'Tech specs' drawer. Manifesto H2 is two-tone (white lead phrase, grey continuation). Isometric wireframe 'FIG 0.x' line illustrations, thin hairline dividers. The only saturated colours are the testimonial cards (pastel blue-lilac gradient and lime #e4f222) and small status/label dots. Pill-shaped buttons (light Sign up/Get started, dark Contact sales). Changelog is a horizontal dot-timeline. Mockup patterns are coded with moderate confidence because they are illustrative.
